stories.h: Canada signals restraint after the latest US trade escalation
stories.w: Prime Minister Mark Carney called Washington's newest import restrictions relatively modest and indicated Ottawa may hold off on further retaliation, reducing the immediate risk of another tariff round.

stories.h: Canada plans a major drone-production push for Ukraine
stories.w: Ottawa said it will scale from roughly 2,000 military drones to millions, send a third of domestic production to Ukraine, and provide new air-defence and energy support before winter.

stories.h: The United States marks 25 years since the September 11 attacks
stories.w: Memorials added a new moment of silence for people who later died from illnesses linked to toxic dust, underscoring the attacks' continuing human and political consequences.

stories.h: Brazil's Supreme Court cancels sessions as its internal crisis deepens
stories.w: The court halted a second consecutive deliberation amid allegations involving justices, police and a failed bank, pushing an institutional dispute into the final weeks before national elections.

stories.h: US terrorist designations reshape the campaign against Latin American gangs
stories.w: Washington's list has grown to 21 Latin American and Caribbean groups, with Ecuador's Los Tiguerones the latest addition, expanding the legal and military framework used against organized crime.

stories.h: Poland warns of more Russian provocations along Ukraine's European borders
stories.w: Prime Minister Donald Tusk said incidents near Polish and Moldovan crossings could foreshadow a broader campaign, while acknowledging that evidence for Russian involvement in one episode was not presented.

stories.h: Sweden votes with a far-right party closer than ever to government
stories.w: More than eight million voters will choose between rival blocs on Sunday, with the Sweden Democrats positioned for cabinet posts for the first time if the right retains power.

stories.h: Fire kills at least 24 students in rebel-held eastern Congo
stories.w: A blaze spread from a wooden home into two schools in densely populated Bukavu, trapping children and injuring dozens in a city controlled by the Rwanda-backed M23 movement.

stories.h: US backs a $100 million telecom expansion in Angola
stories.w: The US Export-Import Bank loan will finance American and European network equipment for Africell, a direct effort to counter Huawei's dominant role in African mobile infrastructure.

stories.h: Gambia promises emergency power additions after blackout protests
stories.w: President Adama Barrow pledged 24 megawatts of new generation by October and a 50-megawatt solar plant after outages lasting up to 48 hours triggered violent demonstrations months before an election.

stories.h: Philippine ferry fire death toll rises to 35
stories.w: Fifty-four people remained missing after flames engulfed a passenger ferry near Palawan; rescuers recovered more bodies while investigators had yet to determine the cause.

stories.h: Houthis seize a strategic island at the entrance to the Red Sea
stories.w: The capture near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait opens a new front in the Iran war and threatens the shipping route Saudi Arabia increasingly relies on as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.h: Putin and Modi meet before an 11-nation BRICS summit
stories.w: India and Russia discussed defence, energy and diplomacy as New Delhi hosts a bloc representing about half the world's population while balancing ties with Moscow and Western partners.

stories.h: Queensland loses a credit-rating notch ahead of Olympic spending
stories.w: S&P cut the state's long-term rating from AA+ to AA, citing weak budgets and structurally higher debt as infrastructure spending rises before the 2032 Brisbane Games.

stories.h: Oil shock wipes $32 billion from Australia's share market
stories.w: Every ASX sector finished lower as crude above $100 revived inflation and interest-rate fears, with the benchmark ending down one percent after a steeper intraday fall.

stories.h: Varroa mite makes a 1,000-kilometre jump into Far North Queensland
stories.w: Authorities confirmed Australia's northernmost detections of the destructive bee parasite and suspect human-assisted hive movement, raising risks for pollination-dependent agriculture.
